items.title: We’ve partnered with Google DeepMind to launch their Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) evaluation, a new benchmark for ag
items.summary:
We’ve partnered with Google DeepMind to launch their Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) evaluation, a new benchmark for agentic knowledge work over complex visual files

@GoogleDeepMind’s MKA is a new benchmark requiring agents to review visually complex project files such as schematics and scans, and produce deliverables like slide decks, spreadsheets, reports, and marked-up images

Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) overview:

➤ 200 private real-world visual tasks across 10 industries: Agents work from dense visual project files including architectural drawings, engineering schematics, and clinical scans to produce deliverables including slide decks, spreadsheets, PDFs, Word documents, and marked-up images. Unlike many agentic evaluations, these inputs emphasize realistic visual complexity and domain-specificity, and are genuinely required to complete the task rather than just providing additional context

➤ Climb vs. Regression rubric scoring: Each task is graded against expert rubrics, averaging ~70 weighted criteria per task. Criteria are split into ‘Regression’ (baseline checks models should pass) and ‘Climb’ criteria (harder checks designed to separate strong models). The headline score is Climb WSR (Weighted Satisfaction Rate) - the weighted proportion Climb rubric criteria successfully completed

➤ Evaluated in Stirrup with an agentic judge: We run every task in Stirrup, our open source agent harness, with code execution, web search, web fetch, and image-viewing tools (up to 250 turns), and grade submitted deliverables using GPT-6 Luna (medium) as an agentic judge

Key MKA results:

➤ Claude Fable 5.2 leads on multimodal knowledge work: Anthropic’s recently released Claude Fable 5.2 (max) leads the MKA leaderboard with a Climb WSR of 57%, followed by Gemini 4 Carbon (high) at 54% and Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 53%

➤ Cost per Task spans nearly 30× within 10 points of the top score: Claude Fable 5.2 averages $31.97 per task, over 5× Gemini 4 Carbon ($6.29) for ~2 extra points, and ~29× GPT-6.1 Sol ($1.11). Below Carbon, all four OpenAI models tested sit on the cost-performance Pareto frontier (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and GPT-6 Luna), with Claude Haiku 5.5 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro making up the rest of the frontier

➤ No single model leads across all 10 industry verticals: Claude Fable 5.2 leads five verticals (Software & Data, Engineering, Logistics & Mapping, Business, and Finance alongside Claude Sonnet 5.5), Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads Education and Construction, Gemini 4 Argon (high) leads Science, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) leads Healthcare, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) narrowly leads Law & Government

Thank you to the @GoogleDeepMind team for their work building this benchmark and collaborating with us to bring it exclusively to Artificial Analysis!

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

items.title: Why the Credit Default Swap Market—Red Hot in the AI Trade—Is Vital for CFOs - WSJ
items.summary:
The rush by investors to take out insurance on their massive AI trades has put a spotlight on a market that CFOs rely on for signals about how investors perceive them. [...] CDS spreads—the price investors pay for the insurance—have widened for AI companies relative to the broader market index. “At a high level, spreads appear to be inconsistent with the large market caps in the equity market,” Patel said, pointing to hyperscalers’ size. Investors need to be compensated for the uncertainty surrounding companies’ AI funding needs, he said.

Copyright ©2026 Dow Jones & Company, Inc. All Rights Reserved. 87990cbe856818d5eddac44c7b1cdeb8 [...] Investors use credit default swaps to hedge existing exposure to an issuer, or to express a view on its credit risk without necessarily holding its debt. Following a massive borrowing spree by hyperscalers to build out AI infrastructure, market participants have taken out more protection on their trades against borrower default. That means buying more CDS contracts.

items.summary: Điểm đáng chú ý của khóa học là sự gắn kết giữa yêu cầu đào tạo chuyên môn với nhu cầu sử dụng cán bộ của địa phương. Việc cử cán bộ đi học không chỉ nhằm bổ sung văn bằng mà hướng đến trang bị kiến thức, kỹ năng để trực tiếp tham mưu, triển khai và giải quyết những vấn đề thực tiễn về công nghệ thông tin, chuyển đổi số tại cơ sở. [...] Việc khai giảng 2 lớp đào tạo đại học Công nghệ thông tin cho cán bộ, công chức cấp xã là bước triển khai cụ thể trong đổi mới công tác đào tạo, bồi dưỡng cán bộ của tỉnh Nghệ An theo hướng xuất phát từ yêu cầu thực tiễn, gắn đào tạo với vị trí việc làm và nhu cầu sử dụng cán bộ. [...] Đối với các học viên, đồng chí đề nghị xác định rõ trách nhiệm học tập, phát huy tinh thần chủ động, cầu thị; gắn kiến thức được đào tạo với những vấn đề thực tiễn đang đặt ra tại cơ quan, đơn vị. Mỗi học viên cần phấn đấu không chỉ sử dụng thành thạo công nghệ mà còn có khả năng tham mưu, đề xuất giải pháp, hướng dẫn đồng nghiệp, trở thành lực lượng nòng cốt thúc đẩy chuyển đổi số tại địa phương.

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

Investors need to be compensated for the uncertainty surrounding companies’ AI funding needs, he said.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Path Robotics raised $300 million at a $2.45 billion valuation
items.summary:
Path Robotics, which builds programs that guide self-operating factory robots, raised $300 million in a Series E round that puts its valuation at $2.45 billion, according to Bloomberg. The valuation is close to four times its previous level. [...] Founded in 2018, the company has centered its work on its Obsidian physical AI model, which gives robotic arms and quadrupeds the ability to weld upwards of 12 different parts, according to Bloomberg. The model lets robots perceive their surroundings, think through problems and adjust on the fly, rather than executing a fixed set of instructions. [...] Path Robotics has 50 advance orders to deliver for Rove, a welding robot that pairs Boston Dynamics’ Spot quadruped with Path Robotics’ technology, according to Bloomberg. According to the startup, the robot is set to join human welders at shipyards, construction sites and large industrial campuses beginning next year.

Customers include U.S. shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls$HII Industries and Saronic Technologies, a maker of maritime drones and unmanned military ships, according to Bloomberg.

items.title: Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing
items.summary:
At the center of Path’s technology is Obsidian, a physical AI welding model that uses real-world production data to help robots identify weld joints, plan and execute welds, and adapt to changing conditions, according to the company.

Path recently introduced Rove, a mobile welding system that pairs Obsidian with a four-legged robot. The system is designed to bring welding capabilities directly to a part rather than requiring the work to take place inside a stationary robotic cell. [...] Share

 Path Robotics raises $300M at $2.45B valuation to scale physical AI for manufacturing 

Path Robotics co-founders and brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (Photo: Path Robotics)

  

Columbus-based Path Robotics has raised $300 million in Series E financing at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation to expand its robotic welding business and bring its artificial intelligence technology to more manufacturing tasks. [...] Path’s expansion targets a production challenge: manufacturers with demand for more products but limited capacity to build them.

The company develops physical AI—technology that enables robots to perceive their surroundings and adapt their actions to changing conditions. Its initial focus has been welding, where variations in parts and joints can make conventional, preprogrammed automation difficult to deploy.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: You could manually program a robot to do a handful of tasks in a factory without issue—this type of automation has been common for decades. Gemini Robotics is not trying to just do a few things, though. These are intended to be general robots that can handle almost anything, but there are trade-offs to that approach. [...] Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.
